## 1. Epidemiological Context: The Hyper-Humid Chocó & Transboundary Basins

The Pacific coastal plains of **Colombia** (Nariño, Chocó, Valle del Cauca) and **Ecuador** (Esmeraldas, El Oro, Guayas) form one of the wettest biogeographic corridors in the world. 

Epidemiological challenges include:
- High precipitation ($>4,000\text{ mm/year}$) leading to chronic soil waterlogging.
- Simultaneous circulation of arboviruses (Dengue, Chikungunya) and malaria (*Anopheles albimanus* and *An. darlingi*).
- Complex transboundary river corridors (e.g., Mira, Mataje) with palafitic houses erected along tidal or fluvial floodplains.

## 2. Targeted Indicator Suite

| Indicator | Implementation | Entomological Significance |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **IEV** | `d4h_iev()` | Vectorial Stagnation Index: detects areas where flat topography ($\text{slope} \approx 0$) coincides with persistent surface moisture. |
| **VARI / EVI** | `d4h_vari()`, `d4h_evi()` | Captures vegetation vigor from standard RGB sensors in high cloud-cover conditions where infrared may saturate. |
| **TWI** | `d4h_twi()` | Identifies natural hydrologic flow paths and subterranean water accumulation in lowlands. |
| **IRHE** | `d4h_irhe()` | Stagnant Turbid Moisture Index: differentiates clean flowing river channels from eutrophic, brackish puddles favored by vector larvae. |

## 3. End-to-End Execution Workflow

```r
library(drones4health)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)

# File paths
path_dem <- "data/choco_pacific/Ohuay_D.tif"    # DEM / DSM
path_nir <- "data/choco_pacific/Ohuay_NIR.tif"  # NIR
path_r   <- "data/choco_pacific/Ohuay_R.tif"    # Red
path_g   <- "data/choco_pacific/Ohuay_G.tif"    # Green
path_rgb <- "data/choco_pacific/Ohuay_D.tif"    # Orthomosaic

# Step 1: Compute Topographic Wetness and Slope
r_slope <- d4h_slope(dem_raster = path_dem, unit = "degrees")
r_twi   <- d4h_twi(dem_raster = path_dem)

# Step 2: Compute Stagnant Moisture Risk (IRHE)
r_irhe  <- d4h_irhe(red = path_r, green = path_g)

# Step 3: Compute Vectorial Stagnation Index (IEV)
r_ndwi  <- d4h_ndwi(green = path_g, nir = path_nir)
r_iev   <- d4h_iev(ndwi = r_ndwi, slope = r_slope)

# Step 4: Visual analytics comparison using interactive swipe
# Compares topographic accumulation (TWI) directly against stagnant moisture (IRHE)
# d4h_mapview_swipe(r_twi, r_irhe)

# Step 5: Executive multi-moment summary
summary_tbl <- d4h_executive_summary(r_iev, by = "general")
print(summary_tbl)
```

## 4. Cross-Border Health Coordination

- **Bi-national Surveillance:** Harmonized metrics between Colombia and Ecuador allow health ministries to compare larval exposure and risk levels along shared riverways using identical quantitative thresholds.
- **Micro-Drainage Infrastructure:** Identify critical drainage choke points where municipal interventions (digging small gravity runoff channels) can eliminate chronic pooling without costly chemical larviciding.
